affectedPublicSurfaces: PROCESS STARTUP for BOTH `juli-api` and the Celery worker (`juli-celery-worker`) — the highest-blast-radius surface in the repo. Both import `assert_agent_runtime_config()` (`workers/agent_runtime_boot.py`) and run it at boot, so a wrong assertion in EITHER direction is an outage: too strict refuses to start a healthy process; too loose lets the production-write capability come up against a database it can bypass — the precondition silently skipped, which is the exact state the whole W7 chain exists to prevent.

The 7th check added to `assert_agent_runtime_config()`: when the production-write capability is ENABLED, the process verifies at boot that (a) its own live connection role is NOT an owner of any table in the runtime schemas, and (b) `relrowsecurity` is true for every table the classification map (from #1329) calls tenant-scoped. Either unmet ⇒ refuse to start, NAMING the check, and for the RLS case NAMING which table. Same shape as the existing check 6 (production-write capability ⇒ zero unauthenticated route groups), applied to the precondition that actually matters.

The capability-gated no-op path: with the production-write capability OFF, the new check does nothing, so today's deployed configuration (process connects as the owner `postgres`, RLS present-but-inert) boots unchanged. This is the case that protects the current deployment and must not break.

The cutover runbook (operator-facing documentation, not runtime code): the out-of-band `GRANT juli_app TO <login>` step from #1326, the `DATABASE_URL` change to name `juli_app`, the two verification commands, and the revert — stating plainly that the revert is a `DATABASE_URL` change and that `alembic downgrade` is NEVER the rollback for a role cutover.

candidateVerificationJourney.restrictedRoute: Pre-merge: pytest with PYTHONPATH pinned to the worktree's backend/src, exercising the boot assertion against a REAL Postgres 16 whose role/RLS state is set up per case (owner vs non-owner connection; full vs partial RLS) — no live host contact. Post-deploy candidate: boot both juli-api and juli-celery-worker with the production-write capability OFF (today's configuration) and confirm a clean start plus one served authenticated read — the no-op case that protects the current deployment; then, on the candidate only, boot with the capability ON against the owner (postgres) connection and confirm the NAMED refusal. No public traffic is routed to a candidate, and the DATABASE_URL cutover itself is NOT performed here (gate #1339 observation 1, an owner act).
candidateVerificationJourney.notes: workersDisabledOnCandidate is FALSE deliberately: the assertion runs at WORKER boot as well as API boot, and the worker half is exactly what a too-strict or too-loose check would break, so the worker must boot in the candidate verification. No production credential is resolved and no write is attempted — this slice only gates startup; it performs neither the DATABASE_URL cutover nor any production mutation. The check must query the LIVE connection's actual role and privileges (pg_catalog: role ownership via pg_class.relowner/pg_roles, and relrowsecurity per tenant-scoped table), NOT a config value describing them — a boot check that asserts a setting is PRESENT rather than EFFECTIVE is the #1282 failure repeated. Both directions are proven: refuse-to-boot (capability on + owner connection, and capability on + one tenant-scoped table's RLS disabled → names the table), and clean-boot (capability off as owner with partial RLS = today's config; and capability on + non-owner + full RLS).

journeys.name: prod-write-capability-refuses-to-boot-against-a-bypassable-db
assertions: pre-merge: with the production-write capability ENABLED and the live connection OWNING tables, assert_agent_runtime_config() raises and refuses boot, and the message NAMES the check — asserted for BOTH the API boot path and the worker boot path, since both import the assertion

pre-merge: with the capability ENABLED and exactly one tenant-scoped table's relrowsecurity disabled on a real Postgres, the process refuses to boot and the message NAMES WHICH table — a check that says only 'RLS is not fully enabled' is one somebody will later disable, so the named-table assertion is explicit

pre-merge: with the capability OFF, the check is a NO-OP — proven by booting as the OWNER (postgres) with RLS partially enabled and observing a clean start, because this is exactly today's deployed configuration and it must not break
pre-merge: with the capability ENABLED, a NON-OWNER connection (juli_app), and full RLS on every classified tenant-scoped table, the process BOOTS cleanly

pre-merge: the check reads the LIVE connection's actual role and privileges from pg_catalog (role ownership and relrowsecurity), NOT a config/env value describing them — a test proves that flipping only the config while the live DB state stays bypassable still refuses (present vs effective; the #1282 failure not repeated)

pre-merge: the tenant-scoped table set the check verifies is the SAME classification source #1329 enumerates from the catalog — not a second hand-maintained list — so a newly-added tenant-scoped table is covered by the boot check without a code edit

The DATABASE_URL cutover to juli_app is NOT performed (owner act, gate #1339 obs 1)

htmlRoutes: No HTML route, page, bundle, or static asset changes — the diff is backend Python (workers/agent_runtime_boot.py plus tests) and a Markdown runbook. The only operator-facing surface is the named boot-refusal message and the runbook.

migrationCompatibility.notes: No migration. The change is a capability-gated boot assertion plus a runbook. It is additive and invisible while the production-write capability is OFF (today's deployment), so the previous release and the new one coexist against the same schema. This slice does NOT perform the DATABASE_URL role cutover — that is gate #1339 observation 1 and an owner act; it only makes the wrong ordering impossible by refusing to boot the capability against a database the connection can bypass.

rollbackAssertion.preCutoverFailureBehavior: Do not merge. Without this check, enabling the production-write capability against a connection that bypasses RLS (owner connection, or a tenant-scoped table with RLS off) would come up silently — the exact unsafe state the chain exists to prevent, with nothing to notice it. No production write is possible today regardless (capability off; ADR-068 guards hold), so there is no new exposure from NOT merging — only the safety gate is absent.
rollbackAssertion.postCutoverFailureBehavior: The check is additive and capability-gated. Revert by removing the 7th check; boot returns to unconditional (its prior behaviour). Assert the revert does NOT leave the capability flag readable-but-unchecked — i.e. reverting must remove the flag's enforcement together with the check, never leave a state where PRODUCTION_WRITE_ENABLED can be read while nothing verifies the DB is non-bypassable, which would be the precondition silently gone. A too-strict assertion is the worse failure: it refuses to start a healthy process, an outage; the clean-boot cases (capability off as owner; capability on + non-owner + full RLS) are the guardrails against that and must stay green.

acceptanceCommands: DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres@localhost:5432/juli_boot_1330 PYTHONPATH=$PWD/backend/src python -m pytest tests -k 'boot and (prod_write or rls or owner or capability)' -q
ruff check backend tests && ruff format --check backend tests
doNotInfer: The check queries the LIVE connection's ACTUAL role and privileges from pg_catalog (role ownership and relrowsecurity), NOT a config value describing them. A boot check that asserts a setting is PRESENT rather than EFFECTIVE is the #1282 failure repeated and is explicitly forbidden.

Refusal NAMES the check, and for the RLS case NAMES which table. A check that says only 'RLS is not fully enabled' is one somebody will later disable; the named-table message is the deliverable, not a nicety.

The check is a NO-OP when the production-write capability is OFF, PROVEN by booting as the owner (postgres) with RLS partially enabled and observing a clean start — this is exactly today's deployed configuration and must not break. Assert BOTH API and worker boot paths, since both import the assertion.

This slice does NOT perform the DATABASE_URL cutover to juli_app — that is gate #1339 observation 1 and an owner act. It makes the cutover safe and reversible and makes the wrong order (capability on before isolation is real) impossible.
Do NOT edit core/security/dependencies.py — W6's #1313 owns that module. Do not edit migration 043 (its no-DELETE grant decision stands) or migration 045.

The tenant-scoped table set the check verifies MUST come from the same classification source #1329 enumerates from the catalog, never a second hand-maintained literal list — so a new tenant-scoped table is covered without a code edit.

The runbook documents the out-of-band GRANT juli_app TO <login> from #1326, the DATABASE_URL change, the two verification commands, and the revert, and states plainly that a downgrade of #1326's migration must be preceded by cutting DATABASE_URL back to postgres — alembic downgrade is NEVER the rollback for a role cutover.
